name: Chief Justice William R. Wooton
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's application of the "mandate rule" was hyper-technical and foreclosed consideration of the petitioner's claim that a BB gun is not a "firearm or other deadly weapon," which he believed merited closer consideration.

name: JUSTICE TRUMP
description: Recused himself from the case.

name: BUNN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court did not err in affirming Mr. Small's convictions and sentence.

name: JUDGE PATRICK WILSON
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: TRUMP, JUSTICE.
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court clearly erred in refusing to impose a recidivist life sentence because neither the disproportionate sentencing nor the substantive due process (selective prosecution) theories validated the circuit court's decision.

name: ARMSTEAD, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court correctly found that the petitioner knowingly and intelligently waived his right to counsel and that there was no reasonable likelihood of correcting the conditions of abuse and neglect, thus affirming the termination of parental rights.

name: Chief Justice, Tim Armstead
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: Justice Elizabeth D. Walker
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: Justice John A. Hutchison
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: Wooton, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the petitioner's equal protection argument deserves more than cursory treatment and is antithetical to the constitutional guarantee of equal protection.

name: BUNN, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the case should have been set for oral argument and that the petitioner's equal protection rights argument should be fully addressed in a signed opinion, given the disparate treatment compared to the Lane case.

name: Chief Justice Tim Armstead
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: Justice William R. Wooton
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: Justice C. Haley Bunn
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: Justice Elizabeth D. Walker
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision gives approval to a 'sue me if you don't like it' approach that offends the balance between municipal rights and property owners' fundamental rights, and that tort actions are an inadequate alternative to inverse condemnation.

name: Justice John A. Hutchison
description: Dissented, joined Justice Walker's dissenting opinion.

name: WALKER, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that while the circuit court erred in failing to credit the defendant for the full time served, the error was harmless because the defendant ultimately received full credit in Raleigh County.

name: WOOTON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Special Acts requiring Cabell County to include library and park funding on its excess levy proposals violate equal protection guarantees because they create a discriminatory classification among counties without a compelling state interest.

name: Justice William R. Wooton
description: Concurred, argued that the 2018 amendment to the burglary statute has a constitutional defect because its title failed to provide proper notice of the removal of the 'of another' requirement, but agreed the defect was harmless in this specific case.

name: HUTCHISON JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the 2020 recidivist statute did not violate ex post facto principles as it did not increase punishment or lengthen the sentence compared to the 2000 statute, and the life sentence was constitutionally proportionate because all three felony offenses involved actual or threatened violence.

name: ARMSTEAD, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the West Virginia Constitution allows the Legislature to enact additional educational initiatives like the Hope Scholarship Act, which does not impinge on the fundamental right to education or improperly direct public funds.

name: JUSTICE WOOTON
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE HUTCHISON
description: Dissented, argued that the Hope Scholarship Act is unconstitutional because the West Virginia Constitution limits the Legislature to providing education through a system of free schools and the Act fails strict scrutiny review by diverting funds from public education.

name: HUTCHISON CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court completely lacked jurisdiction to review as-applied challenges to WVSSAC rules and clearly erred in finding the Residence-Transfer Rule facially unconstitutional, as it meets the rational basis test by promoting academics over athletics and does not violate equal protection.

name: JUSTICE WOOTON
description: Recused himself from the decision.

name: JUDGE COURRIER
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: HUTCHISON, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the mid-deliberation juror substitution violated Rule 24(c) and the trial court failed to take extraordinary precautions to overcome the presumption of prejudice, thus requiring reversal and a new trial.

name: ARMSTEAD, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the defendant was not prejudiced by the juror substitution and received a fair trial, so the convictions should be affirmed.

name: Wooton, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court's failure to re-administer the juror oath to the recalled alternate juror was a fundamental, structural error that rendered the conviction invalid.

name: Chief Justice John A. Hutchison

name: Judge Richard A. Facemire

name: Justice William R. Wooton
description: Deemed himself disqualified and did not participate.

name: ARMSTEAD, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that claims for excessive force by police officers under the West Virginia Constitution must be analyzed under the specific search and seizure clause (Article III, Section 6) and not the general due process clause (Article III, Section 10), and that claims under Section 10 are redundant as no private right of action for monetary damages exists under Section 6.

name: JUSTICE ALAN D. MOATS
description: Not participating in the decision.

name: Armstead, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Judge Goldston's actions constituted an unlawful search and an exercise of executive power, violating the Code of Judicial Conduct and warranting censure and a $1,000 fine.

name: JUSTICE WOOTON
description: Dissented, argued that while discipline was warranted, the conduct was more a legal error than an ethical violation, and an admonishment with a $1,000 fine would be more appropriate, deferring to the Judicial Hearing Board's recommendation.

name: JUSTICE HUTCHISON
description: Disqualified himself from the decision.

name: HUTCHISON, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that prior decisions (Hall and Divita) were incorrectly decided by automatically reversing revocation orders for an officer's failure to provide a blood test, and that a new test should evaluate the violation in the context of the entire record.

name: WOOTON, J.
description: Dissented, arguing that the majority's new point of law is a dangerous exercise in futility, improperly creates judicial restraints on a legislatively prescribed due process right, and may invite misapplication in future criminal DUI proceedings, especially given the imminent termination of the administrative revocation procedure.

name: WALKER, Justice
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: JENKINS, Chief Justice
description: Dissented from the denial of the writ regarding the 2015 Act's applicability and the striking of non-party fault notices, and concurred in part and dissented in part regarding the jury trial issue.

name: ARMSTEAD, Justice
description: Concurred that a jury trial is needed for intertwined claims but dissented because the majority denied defendants their statutory right to allocate fault under the 2015 Act, which should apply to claims seeking monetary compensation.

name: HUTCHISON, Justice
description: Concurred, praising the majority for addressing the complex opioid crisis litigation and upholding the right to jury trials while allowing the trial panel flexibility.

name: WOOTON, Justice
description: Concurred that a writ of prohibition was not warranted for the bench trial decision but dissented from the majority's intervention in the early stages of litigation and its analysis, arguing it gave too much credence to premature legal arguments.

name: WALKER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that an EPO is not a de facto search warrant and does not authorize law enforcement to search a home for firearms, and no other warrant exception applied to validate the entry and search.

name: ARMSTEAD, J.
description: Concurred that an EPO is not equivalent to search and seizure authority but dissented from reversing the conviction, arguing the record requires further development on whether there was implied consent for officers to enter the home.
